newsitem.title: CHINA: Guangzhou has fund shortage, to curb investment.
newsitem.headline: Guangzhou has fund shortage, to curb investment.

text.p: Authorities in the big south China city of Guangzhou will curb investment in major projects next year because of a shortage of funds, the Business Weekly newspaper said on Sunday.
It said that investment in key projects will be held to 12 billion yuan ($1.45 billion) next year compared with 11.9 billion this year.

"In view of the city's capability, total investment in the large projects in 1997 will be maintained at the current level," the newspaper quoted Huang Guangyu, deputy director of the Guangzhou Municipal Planning Commission as saying.
The newspaper said the city had as much as a 70 percent shortfall in its investment funds for some of the 12 key projects as of October.
The city had poured funds into its new railway station and four more of the key projects but there were serious funding gaps for the other seven.
The newspaper also said that a new steel plant and an expansion for an automobile plant have been held up, awaiting central government approval. It gave no further details.
